evidence.approach: F1 from the attempt 5 review: a test-only change under packages/core/src is held to no floor, because mutation.source_files() and mutation_ci.select() both drop test files. One mapping function in harness/mutation.py, under_test(path, exists), answers which source a test file covers: for packages/core/src/<x>.test.ts or <x>.spec.ts its sibling <x>.ts when that file exists, otherwise the test's own directory (which mutation.command already expands into the globs of the files under it, tests left out). exists is a predicate over repository paths, so the function stays pure and testable. source_files(paths, exists) applies it, so a slice naming only a test still yields a source entry, and both callers that already use source_files (gates.plan_source_files, which the mutation command reads, and gates._require_mutation, which holds the floor) pass a predicate over the repository root. mutation_ci.select() stops filtering tests itself and calls mutation.source_files with a predicate over the checkout (CI runs it from the repository root), then turns the entries into the --mutate value through a new mutation.patterns(entries), which command() also uses, so the gate, the mutation command and CI cannot disagree on either the mapping or the globs. The config-change rule (all of src) is unchanged. The lows ride along in slice 2: F3, report._mutation says not applicable only when not_applicable is true and otherwise 'not measured: <reason>', and kpi.mutation reads only the measurements of the ticket's last attempt that took any, so a failed attempt-2 run is not carried as attempt 3's figure; F4, the Outcome drops the CI run figure no record holds and quotes only what a journal record carries. F2 and F5 need nothing (F2 is the clarify record 6 decision, F5 is settled by the qa check).
changes: harness/mutation.py: under_test(path, exists) maps a test under packages/core/src to its sibling source or its directory; source_files(paths, exists) applies it instead of dropping tests; patterns(entries) holds the file and directory to glob expansion that command() and CI share.

harness/mutation_ci.py: select(changed_paths, exists) delegates to mutation.source_files and mutation.patterns; main() passes a predicate over the working directory; the module docstring states the mapping.
harness/gates.py: plan_source_files(records, root) and _require_mutation pass a predicate over the repository root to mutation.source_files.
harness/cli.py: the mutation command passes the repository root to gates.plan_source_files.
harness/tests/test_mutation.py: SourceFilesTest gains the sibling and the directory mappings; the gate tests gain a slice naming only a test that is refused without a measurement.
harness/tests/test_mutation_ci.py: test_only_test_files_select_nothing is replaced by the test that a changed test selects its sibling, and its directory when it has none.
harness/report.py and harness/kpi.py: F3, a null score reads not applicable only when not_applicable is true, and the kpi reads the last attempt that measured.
docs/tickets/SEEN-116-property-based-and-mutation-tests-on-the-money.md: F4, the Outcome quotes only figures a record holds, and attempt 6 is described.
docs/harness/workflow.md: one sentence that a test-only change is measured over the source it tests.

slices.name: A test-only change is measured over the source it tests, in the gate and in CI
slices.red: source_files over a slice naming only packages/core/src/fees/detect.test.ts returns nothing, so the gate advances with no measurement; select over a changed test returns None, so CI skips the job.

slices.name: The report and the kpi say not measured for a run that measured nothing, and the Outcome quotes only recorded figures
slices.red: A failed measurement (null score, not_applicable false) renders as not applicable, and kpi.mutation returns an earlier attempt's measurement when the last attempt took none.

alternatives: Map a test to its directory always: rejected, it mutates every file beside a sibling-tested source and costs CI time for files the test does not touch; the sibling is the repository's convention and the directory is only the fallback.

Read the test's imports to find what it covers: rejected, it needs a TypeScript resolver in Python for a gain the sibling convention already gives; Stryker's own per-test coverage then decides which mutants the test kills.
Leave the mapping in each caller: rejected, the review's point is that the gate and CI must not disagree, so there is one function.
Split F1 into a follow-up ticket: rejected by Ruud's decision at record 78.
risks: A test file that tests a source elsewhere (not its sibling, not its directory) is measured over the wrong files and its weakening still escapes: mitigated by the convention, and the directory fallback widens rather than narrows what is measured.

Mutating a whole directory for a test with no sibling makes the CI step slower: the ten-minute criterion is re-measured on this pull request's CI run, and the directory fallback is rare under the sibling convention.
exists checks the working tree, so a test whose sibling the branch deleted maps to the directory: that is the intended reading, the source no longer exists to be measured.
evidence.rollback: Revert the commits of attempt 6; the mapping only adds entries to what the gate and CI measure, so reverting returns to attempt 5's behaviour with no data to migrate.
